chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Talha, who linked it up through his chain to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
He said: The angels are in three parts; one part has two wings, one part has three wings, and one part has four wings.
ai.seo_question: How many wings do angels have according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the physical diversity of angels, categorizing them into three groups based on their wing count: two, three, or four. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of angelic hierarchy and variation in creation, distinguishing these specific physical attributes from the general description of seraphim in the Quran. It serves to illustrate the vastness of God’s creation while maintaining the angels' role as obedient servants.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-191 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Talha who linked it up through a chain of narrators to the Prophet (MGB), “
There are three groups of angels. One group of angels has two wings. Another group of angels has three wings. And a third group of angels has four wings.”
